 Managerial merry-go-round published at 19:51 BST 19:51 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Don't forget that last season the manager role at Nottingham Forest was a bit of a merry-go-round.
 It is just over a year since Ange Postecoglou's 39-day reign ended after six defeats and no wins in eight games.
 Sean Dyche lasted a little over 100 days and while Vitor Pereira took Forest to the Europa League semi-finals and achieved top-flight survival, he was sacked just two minutes before a termination clause expired in June.
 7 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Gibbs-White is our key attacking player' published at 19:49 BST 19:49 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Nottingham Forest 
 Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner talking to Sky Sports about whether you can overthink when results aren't going your way: "Yes, very often. You think about whether we should change here or there. We watch our performances back and we feel like with our performances we could have four, five or six points more. We're not overthinking. Today we will do everything necessary to get the win. 
 "It is proper English weather tonight so I expect a very intense game. This is what we have to match."
 On Morgan Gibbs-White's return: "Morgan is maybe our key player in our attack. He scored 15 goals last season and he's been unlucky this season - I think he could have five, six or seven assists already. For an assist you always need someone who takes the chance! With his creativity, his understanding of the game and his personal goal threat, he is very important for our attack."

 'We just need to be clinical' published at 19:45 BST 19:45 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Nottingham Forest 
 Former Ipswich man Liam Delap, who is now leading the line for Forest, speaking to Sky Sports: "Special place in my heart so glad to be back.
 "I don't think there's a lack of confidence, we just need that one to click and we are proving we are performing really well we just need to be clinical and be ruthless.
 "The first one just needs to come, we are creating chances and I think it's going to happen, it's going to come. We are confident and we believe we can win."

 Where are Forest's goals? published at 19:42 BST 19:42 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Chris Adams 
BBC Sport journalist 
 Liam Delap was Ipswich's top scorer in their previous Premier League campaign in 2024-25. Having scored with his third shot for Forest this term, the £45m summer signing from Chelsea has had a further 15 attempts without success.
 "I don't see it as a massive problem because we're creating enough situations," boss Oliver Glasner said this week in reference to the goalscoring issue, although Forest fans might not entirely agree. 
 The Tricky Trees have failed to score in four different top-flight games this season, with no side drawing a blank more often.

 Glasner has spoken to Marinakis about slow starts published at 19:36 BST 19:36 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Nick Mashiter 
BBC Sport football news reporter 
 There is confidence internally Forest are still on the right track under Oliver Glasner, who has impressed with his methods and personality.
 He was brought in to take Forest to the next level after lifting the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League with Palace.
 Glasner is impatient to repeat that success, detailing how owner Evangelos Marinakis is the only person he has met with more ambition than him.
 The 52-year-old has also said he is not a magician and has already spoken to Marinakis about previous slow starts.
 He won just one of his opening six games at Palace after replacing Roy Hodgson in February 2024 and then did not win any of his first eight games in his first full season with the Eagles in 2024-25.
 That campaign finished with Palace beating Manchester City in the FA Cup final to end a 119-year wait for a first major trophy.

 'Not good enough' published at 19:32 BST 19:32 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Forest boss Oliver Glasner says "five points after seven games is not good enough", but is confident his team "will give everything" to get more on the board in the coming weeks.
 "I never look at the table in October, but of course we want to get more points," Glasner told BBC Radio Nottingham. "I feel we are playing better than the teams I've previously managed in the early stages.
 "The results are the same, but the spirit gives me confidence."

 Is Glasner in trouble already? published at 19:26 BST 19:26 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Oliver Glasner is considered to be Crystal Palace's greatest ever manager having guided them to FA Cup and European Conference glory. 
 But his time at Forest so far has been tough. Seven games, one win. It's a record that sees the Tricky Trees currently 19th in the Premier League.
 And with Forest's owner notoriously impatient, is Glasner in trouble already?

 Faltering Forest need a win published at 19:20 BST 19:20 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Chris Adams 
BBC Sport journalist 
 Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner is one of several Premier League bosses in dire need of a win to stave off the threat of losing his job.
 The Austrian, who moved to the City Ground just 40 days after guiding Crystal Palace to Conference League glory, is already under intense scrutiny after only one win in seven league games.
 Forest have scored just five league goals, fewer than any other team in the division, and sit second-bottom with a tricky run before the November international window. Their xG underperformance of -6.2 is the worst in the division, with marquee summer signing Liam Delap netting just once.
 Forest have lost their past three league games, more defeats than in their previous 14. With last season's top scorer Morgan Gibbs-White fit again for the trip to Suffolk, Glasner will be hoping his men can arrest this worrying decline in form.

 Forest's start raises questions - but belief in Glasner remains published at 19:16 BST 19:16 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Nick Mashiter 
BBC Sport football news reporter 
 "It feels unfair but I don't want to be complaining and feeling as victims."
 Oliver Glasner's words offer a positive outlook as he believes Nottingham Forest deserve more following their disappointing start to the season.
 Tonight's visit to Ipswich comes after three straight defeats during an underwhelming opening which has left them in the Premier League's relegation zone.
 It was not a position they expected to be in after appointing Glasner in the summer, following his exit from Crystal Palace.
 They have been agonisingly close to successful results, wasting golden chances before losing at Palace and nearly hung on for a battling point against champions Arsenal last Sunday. 
 There is belief that progress is being made, but it needs to translate on the pitch.

 Image source, Getty Images Ipswich are already enjoying a more successful stint in the Premier League than the last time they were here (2024-25).
 Should they win tonight they would match the number of wins they had when relegated in 2025.
 They only got seven points at home in that season and avoiding defeat tonight would better that. And it's only October.

 Tractor Boys ploughing on published at 19:04 BST 19:04 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Chris Adams 
BBC Sport journalist 
 One thing Ipswich fans can be assured of is that their team will fight until the end of each game. All three of those wins – over Sunderland, Crystal Palace and Fulham, have come through late winners.
 They also scored consolations at the death in defeats by the two Manchester clubs, meaning their total of five goals netted in the 90th minute or later is more than any other side have managed this term.
 Two of those have come from Zian Flemming. The Dutchman, who was top scorer for relegated Burnley last season, has made an impact since joining from the Clarets for an initial fee of £17m on transfer deadline day, with two goals in five substitute appearances. 
 Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil is unlikely to repeat the 3-4-2-1 system deployed in last week's loss to Manchester City. With midfielder Sasa Lukic hoping to be available again after a groin issue, a return to the usual 4-2-3-1 system is expected against an opponent O'Neil has a decent record against.
 The former Bournemouth and Wolves boss hasn't lost in his five previous Premier League matches against Forest, winning one and drawing four - the most games he has managed against any club without suffering defeat in this competition.

 'Going to be very tight' published at 19:01 BST 19:01 BST 
 Ipswich v Nottm Forest (20:00 BST) 
 Image source, BBC Sport This game is a tough one to call. It is going to be very tight.
 Nottingham Forest can't score. That's their issue, and they have only managed five goals in their first seven league games.
 It did make me laugh when I read that Forest boss Oliver Glasner had got Chris Wood to give advice to the other strikers about finishing - why not just play Wood then?
 Ipswich are still bottom of the league table based on my predictions but they ran Manchester City close in the end last week and are doing better than everyone expected, myself included.
 I like what Tractor Boys boss Gary O'Neil is doing there, and they already have three league wins from seven games - the last time they were in the Premier League, in 2024-25, they only managed four all season.
 Forest are second bottom and could really do with getting something here, and Ipswich haven't drawn a game yet - so that's what I am going for.
 Sutton's prediction: 1-1
